credits_cram.why: Describes CRAM as introduced by \citet{hoover2026cram} ('A recent prominent study ... introduced CRAM') and presents the authors' work as an independent re-implementation, not a new method.

cites_hoover.why: Uses \citet{hoover2026cram} repeatedly in the abstract, introduction, related work and methodology.

small_n.why: States 'we evaluated Opus and Sonnet on 5 puzzles each, and Haiku on 10 puzzles' and the limitations section notes the restricted 5--10 puzzles per model.

handset_caveat.why: Reports the hand-set single-weight energy at 497/500 against learned CRAM at 496--497/500, and says it matches or exceeds the learned model.

their_numbers.why: Attributes 99.996% and 42 ms on an H200 to Hoover et al. ('reported a 42 ms training time on an NVIDIA H200'), and contrasts them with its own 2.52 s CPU fit.

no_new_claims.why: Adds details absent from the log: 12 cores and 24 GB memory, per-model generation times, Haiku max time 189.4 s, a quoted prompt, 'fewer than 800 tokens', and 'proprietary codebase'.
